mainTopic: Using מעות מעשר שני to buy things or to make קידושין: when the deal takes effect, why רבי יהודה lets a deliberate קידושין work, and why a forbidden purchase isn't simply cancelled
overview: This amud opens in the middle of a ברייתא about someone who uses מעות מעשר שני outside ירושלים to buy an animal for שלמים. The תנא קמא says a purchase made by mistake is cancelled and a deliberate one stands. רבי יהודה limits this: if the buyer was really trying to make the holy money ordinary, the purchase is always cancelled. The גמרא asks how this fits our משנה, where רבי יהודה says a deliberate קידושין with מעשר שני works. רבי אלעזר answers that a woman knows the money stays holy, so she accepts it planning to eat it in ירושלים. רבי ירמיה pushes back from the case of buying a non-kosher animal, slaves, or land with מעשר שני money. There people supposedly know the rule too, yet the buyer must eat food of equal value. The גמרא then narrows the answer: our משנה is about an אשה חבירה, who truly knows these laws. Finally the גמרא asks why, in that case of forbidden purchases, the sale isn't simply cancelled as in רבי יהודה's ruling. שמואל begins to answer, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Buying a peace-offering animal with second-tithe money: unknowing versus deliberate
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that if someone bought the animal with מעשר שני money without realizing it, the sale is cancelled. If he did it on purpose, the animal goes up to ירושלים and is eaten there.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he bought it by mistake, the money goes back to where it came from. If he bought it on purpose, the animal is brought up and eaten in ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting a ברייתא about someone who used מעות מעשר שני to buy an animal for שלמים outside ירושלים. It now gives the ruling for a mistaken purchase and for a deliberate one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he did not know the money was מעשר שני, the deal counts as a mistake and is undone. The money stays holy and goes back to the buyer. If he did it on purpose, the deal stands, and the animal takes on the holiness, so it must be brought to ירושלים and eaten there.

keyTerms.meaning: Second-tithe money, holy money that must be spent on food eaten in ירושלים
Unknowingly, by mistake
On purpose, knowingly
The money returns to its place, meaning the sale is cancelled
Peace-offerings

phrases.english: And if he bought it unknowingly,
phrases.notes: He bought an animal for שלמים with מעשר שני money, not realizing which money he was using.

phrases.english: the money returns to its place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא that began before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unknowing purchase with מעשר שני is cancelled; a deliberate purchase stands and the animal is eaten in ירושלים.

steps.title: רבי יהודה limits the ruling to someone who really meant to buy a peace-offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the deliberate purchase stands only if the buyer truly wanted a שלמים. If his real goal was to turn the holy money into ordinary money, the sale is cancelled whether he did it by mistake or on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: When does this apply? When he meant from the start to buy the animal for שלמים. But if he meant to take the מעשר שני money out into ordinary use, then whether by mistake or on purpose, the money goes back to its place.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה narrows the rule of the previous step. A deliberate purchase only stands if the person really wanted the animal as a שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deciding question is what the buyer was trying to do. If he wanted a קרבן, the animal carries the holiness. If he was trying to make the holy money ordinary, which is not allowed this way, the deal does not take effect at all, even if he acted on purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case was this said? A phrase that introduces a limit on a ruling
With the intention of
To take out into ordinary, non-holy status
From the start

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is what clashes with רבי יהודה's view in our משנה, and the rest of the סוגיא depends on it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
In what case are these words said?
When he intended, and bought it from the start for the sake of a peace-offering.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּמִתְכַּוֵּין לְהוֹצִיא מְעוֹת מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי לְחוּלִּין,
phrases.english: But when he intended to take second-tithe money out into ordinary use,
whether unknowingly or on purpose,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the deliberate-purchase ruling of step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the goal was to make מעשר שני money ordinary, the deal is void even when done on purpose.

steps.title: Contradiction from רבי יהודה's view in our משנה
steps.stepSummary: In our משנה, רבי יהודה says that someone who deliberately makes קידושין with מעשר שני has made a valid קידושין. That seems to clash with what he just said in the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn in the משנה: רבי יהודה says that if it was done on purpose, he has made a valid קידושין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction between רבי יהודה in the ברייתא and רבי יהודה in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who gives מעשר שני money for קידושין is using the holy money for something else, just like the buyer in the ברייתא. In the ברייתא רבי יהודה cancels such a deal even when it was deliberate. In the משנה he lets a deliberate קידושין work.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn in a משנה? A phrase that opens a challenge
He has made a valid קידושין

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in the mishna:
Rabbi Yehuda says: if on purpose, he has betrothed her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 2 using רבי יהודה's ruling in our משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling in the ברייתא that a deliberate use of מעשר שני to make it ordinary is void
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In our משנה he holds that a deliberate קידושין with מעשר שני is valid, which looks like the same kind of deal.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: the woman knows the money stays holy
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that a woman knows מעשר שני money does not become ordinary when she takes it. She accepts it planning to go up and eat it in ירושלים, so the קידושין works.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: A woman knows that מעשר שני money does not become ordinary by being given to her, and she will go up and eat it in ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the contradiction by pointing to a difference between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the man wanted to make the holy money ordinary, and that cannot work. In קידושין, the woman knows the money stays מעשר שני and accepts it as is, planning to use it properly in ירושלים. Nobody is trying to change its status, so the קידושין takes effect.

keyTerms.meaning: She knows
Become ordinary, lose their holy status
Through her, by being given to her

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: אִשָּׁה יוֹדַעַת שֶׁאֵין מְעוֹת מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי
phrases.english: A woman knows that second-tithe money
does not become ordinary through her,
and she goes up and eats it in Jerusalem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 3
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Deliberate קידושין with מעשר שני should be void, just like the deliberate attempt to make the money ordinary in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The woman knowingly accepts the money as מעשר שני to eat in ירושלים, so the קידושין is valid.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: people also know the rule for non-kosher animals, slaves and land
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה argues that everyone knows מעשר שני money cannot be spent on a non-kosher animal, slaves, or land. Yet the משנה says that if someone did buy them, he must eat food of equal value himself, so the seller is not treated as accepting the money as מעשר שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה objected: But there are a non-kosher animal, slaves and land, where people know that מעשר שני money does not become ordinary by buying them. And we learned: One may not buy a non-kosher animal, slaves or land with מעשר שני money, even in ירושלים, and if he did buy them, he must eat food of the same value!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה attacks רבי אלעזר's answer. He uses a case where people supposedly know the rule, but the law does not treat the seller as knowingly taking holy money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If "people know the money stays holy" were enough, the seller of these items should count as accepting מעשר שני and should take it to ירושלים himself. Instead the משנה makes the buyer eat food of equal value, which treats the seller as someone who thinks the money became ordinary. So general knowledge of the rule cannot be assumed.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it
A non-kosher animal
Slaves and land
He must eat food matching their value

steps.confusionAlert: "יאכל כנגדן" does not mean he eats the animal or the land. It means the buyer must spend an equal amount of his own money on food and eat it in ירושלים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya objects to this:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אלעזר's answer in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's claim that the woman is assumed to know the money stays holy
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In buying non-kosher animals, slaves or land, people supposedly know the rule too. Yet the seller is not treated as accepting מעשר שני, since the buyer must eat food of equal value.

steps.title: The משנה is about an אשה חבירה who really knows the law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the answer: our משנה is talking about an אשה חבירה, a woman careful about these laws, who truly knows the money stays holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, here we are dealing with an אשה חבירה, who knows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the general claim that every woman knows the rule. It sets the משנה in a narrower case, a woman who is careful about these laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary people cannot be assumed to know these laws, as רבי ירמיה showed. An אשה חבירה does know them, so she knowingly accepts the money as מעשר שני to take to ירושלים, and the קידושין works. That is how רבי יהודה's ruling in the משנה fits his ruling in the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who carefully keeps the laws of purity and tithes
We are dealing with
Who knows

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה's ruling that a deliberate קידושין with מעשר שני works applies to an אשה חבירה. She knows the money stays holy and accepts it to eat in ירושלים. An ordinary person cannot be assumed to know this.

phrases.english: Rather, here
we are dealing with a woman who is a ḥavera, who knows.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Revises step 4's answer in light of the challenge in step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every woman can be assumed to know that מעשר שני money stays holy.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only an אשה חבירה can be assumed to know, and our משנה is about her.

steps.title: Why not cancel the sale and return the money?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ruling 'if he bought, he eats equal value' and asks why the money does not simply go back, like in רבי יהודה's case.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: If he bought them, he must eat food equal to their value. But why? Let the money go back to its place, just like in the case there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ruling quoted in step 5 and challenges it. It asks why the buyer has to make up the value himself instead of the sale being cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (step 2), רבי יהודה said that when someone's real goal was to turn מעשר שני money into ordinary money, the sale is cancelled and the money goes back. Buying a non-kosher animal, slaves, or land with מעשר שני money looks like the same kind of improper use. So why doesn't the same rule apply here, cancelling the sale and returning the money, instead of making the buyer eat food of equal value?

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said.' This phrase brings back a source the גמרא already quoted so it can examine it.
Equal to their value. The buyer must eat food of the same value as holy food in ירושלים.
'But why?' This word opens a challenge.
'Let his money go back to its place.' The sale is cancelled and the seller returns the money.
'Just like there.' It points back to an earlier case.

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: This is quoting the source brought in step 5 about buying forbidden things with מעשר שני money.

phrases.english: If he bought them, he must eat [food] equal to their value.
But why?
Let his money go back to its place,
just like there!
phrases.notes: 'There' means רבי יהודה's ruling from step 2, where the sale was cancelled.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? יַחְזְרוּ דָּמָיו לִמְקוֹמָם, כִּי הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the source quoted in step 5 and compares it with רבי יהודה's ruling from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that one who bought forbidden items with מעשר שני money must eat food of equal value.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In רבי יהודה's case, improper use of מעשר שני money cancels the sale and the money returns. This case seems similar, so the same result should apply instead of making the buyer pay from his own pocket.

steps.title: שמואל begins his answer

steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup: it tells us that שמואל is about to answer the question from step 7. His answer itself continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here we only learn who is answering. שמואל will explain why this case is different from רבי יהודה's case, or how the ruling should be understood, in the next lines.
